document_metadata.document_title: Wet Detention Pond (1001) — WDNR Technical Standard

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Permanent pool surface area sized from post-construction peak outflow during the 1-yr, 24-hour design storm and target particle settling velocity (Equation 1; 80%/60%/40% TSS via 3/6/12 micron particles). Active storage volume above the permanent pool sized with a hydrograph method (TR-55 / App. B) for the 1-yr, 24-hour storm. Demonstrates TSS reduction and peak-flow control per NR 151.12.

evidence.excerpt: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources Technical Standard
This practice provides a method to demonstrate that a wet detention pond achieves the total suspended solids (TSS) reduction and peak flow control required by NR 151.12, Wis. Adm. Code
Technical Standards are reviewed periodically and updated if needed... 10/07
Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources Technical Standard

the peak outflow during the 1-yr., 24-hour design storm... Design the outlet to control the proposed 2-yr., 24-hour discharge... Any storm up to the 10-yr., 24-hour design storm shall not flow backward... Design the spillway to safely pass peak flows produced by a 100-yr., 24-hour design storm
The permanent pool surface area is sized based on the particle size and the peak outflow during the 1-yr., 24-hour design storm using Equation 1: Sa = 1.2 * (qo / vs)
Use a hydrograph-producing method, such as the one outlined in Natural Resources Conservation Service, Technical Release 55 (TR-55), to determine the storage volume for detention ponds.
The post-development outflow shall not exceed pre-development peak flows for the 2-yr., 24-hour design storm. Use a hydrograph-producing method such as TR-55 for all runoff and flow calculations.
Pollutant loading models such as SLAMM, P8, DETPOND or equivalent methodology may also be used to evaluate the efficiency of the design in reducing TSS.
SLAMM and P8 are examples of models that may be used to verify that a detention pond design meets the desired total suspended solids reduction.
Wet Detention Pond (1001)... A permanent pool of water with designed dimensions, inlets, outlets and storage capacity, constructed to collect, detain, treat and release stormwater runoff.

extraction_quality.review_notes: Narrow WDNR Technical Standard 1001 for wet detention ponds only — not a full statewide stormwater design manual. Explicitly excludes flood-control design; local authorities may require peak control beyond the 2-yr, 24-hour storm. SLAMM/P8/DETPOND are approved optional models, not mandated for every design. Companion standards (1002–1004, 1064) and NR 151 govern broader post-construction requirements.
